title_en: Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Cyberspace

articles.content_en: Article 8 Any organization or individual that discovers a violation of the provisions of these Regulations may lodge a complaint or report with the relevant departments such as cyberspace administration, news publication, film, education, telecommunications, public security, civil affairs, culture and tourism, health, market supervision and administration, radio and television, etc. The department that receives the complaint or report shall promptly handle it according to law; if it is not within its duties, it shall promptly transfer it to the department with authority to handle it.

Article 9 Relevant industry organizations of the network shall strengthen industry self-discipline, formulate industry norms related to the online protection of minors, guide their members to perform the obligation of online protection of minors, and strengthen the online protection of minors.

Article 10 News media shall carry out publicity on laws and regulations, policies and measures, typical cases, and relevant knowledge concerning the online protection of minors through news reports, special columns (programs), public service announcements, and other means, conduct public opinion supervision over acts that infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of minors, and guide the whole society to jointly participate in the online protection of minors.

Article 11 The State encourages and supports the strengthening of scientific research and personnel training in the field of online protection of minors, and the conducting of international exchanges and cooperation.

Article 12 Organizations and individuals that have made outstanding contributions in the work of online protection of minors shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Promotion of Network Literacy

Article 13 The education department of the State Council shall incorporate network literacy education into the content of school quality education, and shall, together with the national cyberspace administration department, formulate evaluation indicators for minors' network literacy.
The education department shall guide and support schools in carrying out network literacy education for minors, and cultivate minors' network security awareness, civilized literacy, behavioral habits, and protective skills around the formation of network moral awareness, cultivation of network legal concepts, construction of network use ability, protection of personal and property safety, etc.

Article 14 People's governments at or above the county level shall scientifically plan and rationally distribute, promote the balanced and coordinated development of public interest online services, strengthen the construction of public cultural facilities providing public interest online services, and improve the conditions for minors to access the network.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall provide students with high-quality network literacy education courses by equipping primary and secondary schools with instructors possessing corresponding professional capabilities, government procurement of services, or encouraging primary and secondary schools to purchase relevant services on their own, among other means.

Article 15 Where schools, communities, libraries, cultural centers, youth palaces, and other places provide Internet access service facilities for minors, they shall provide guidance on Internet use and a safe and healthy Internet environment for minors through arranging professionals, recruiting volunteers, and other means, as well as installing network protection software for minors or adopting other safety protection technical measures.

Article 16 Schools shall incorporate content such as improving students' network literacy into educational and teaching activities, and use the network reasonably to carry out teaching activities, establish and improve the management system for students' Internet use during school, manage smart terminal products brought into school by minor students according to law, help students develop good Internet habits, cultivate students' awareness of network security and network rule of law, and enhance students' ability to obtain and analyze network information.

Article 17 The guardians of minors shall strengthen the construction of family education and family tradition, improve their own network literacy, regulate their own behavior of using the network, and strengthen the education, demonstration, guidance, and supervision of minors' behavior of using the network.

Article 18 The State encourages and supports the research, development, production, and use of network protection software, smart terminal products, and network technologies, products, and services such as minor mode and minor zones that are specifically targeted at minors and adapted to the laws and characteristics of minors' physical and mental health development, strengthen the construction and renovation of barrier-free network environments, and promote minors to broaden their horizons, cultivate their sentiments, and improve their quality.

Article 19 Network protection software for minors and smart terminal products specially provided for minors shall have functions such as effectively identifying illegal information and information that may affect the physical and mental health of minors, protecting minors' personal information rights and interests, preventing minors from becoming addicted to the network, and facilitating guardians to perform their guardianship duties.
The national cyberspace administration department shall, together with the relevant departments of the State Council according to the needs of the online protection of minors, clarify the relevant technical standards or requirements for network protection software for minors and smart terminal products specially provided for minors, and guide and supervise the relevant industry organizations of the network to evaluate the use effect of network protection software for minors and smart terminal products specially provided for minors in accordance with the relevant technical standards and requirements.
Manufacturers of smart terminal products shall, before the products leave the factory, install network protection software for minors, or inform users of the installation channels and methods in a conspicuous manner. Sellers of smart terminal products shall, before the sale of products, inform users of the situation of installation of network protection software for minors and the installation channels and methods in a conspicuous manner.
Guardians of minors shall reasonably use and guide minors to use network protection software, smart terminal products, etc., and create a good family environment for network use.

Article 21 The State shall encourage and support the creation, reproduction, publication, and dissemination of online information that promotes socialist core values, advanced socialist culture, revolutionary culture, and fine traditional Chinese culture, strengthens the sense of community for the Chinese nation, fosters minors' feelings of patriotism and good moral character, and guides minors to develop good living habits and behavioral habits, thereby creating a clean cyberspace and a sound online ecosystem conducive to the healthy growth of minors.

Article 22 No organization or individual may produce, reproduce, publish, or disseminate online information that contains content advocating obscenity, pornography, violence, cults, superstition, gambling, inducing self-harm or suicide, terrorism, separatism, extremism, or other content harmful to the physical and mental health of minors.
No organization or individual may produce, reproduce, publish, disseminate, or hold any obscene or pornographic online information concerning minors.

Article 23 Where online products and services contain information that may cause or induce minors to imitate unsafe behaviors, commit acts violating social morality, develop extreme emotions, or develop unhealthy habits, or other information that may affect the physical and mental health of minors, the organization or individual that produces, reproduces, publishes, or disseminates such information shall give prominent prompts before the information is displayed.
The national cyberspace administration department shall, together with the national news publication, film departments, and the departments of education, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television under the State Council, on the basis of the preceding paragraph, determine the specific categories, scope, judgment criteria, and prompting methods for information that may affect the physical and mental health of minors.

Article 24 No organization or individual may produce, reproduce, publish, or disseminate information specified in the first paragraph of Article 23 of these Regulations that may affect the physical and mental health of minors in online products and services specifically targeted at minors.
Online product and service providers may not place information specified in the first paragraph of Article 23 of these Regulations that may affect the physical and mental health of minors at prominent positions such as homepage first screens, pop-ups, or trending searches, or other key links within the product or service that are conspicuous and likely to attract users' attention.
Online product and service providers may not conduct commercial marketing to minors through automated decision-making methods.

Article 25 No organization or individual may send or push, or induce or compel minors to access, online information containing content harmful or potentially harmful to the physical and mental health of minors.

Article 26 No organization or individual may engage in cyberbullying against minors through the internet in the form of text, images, audio, or video, such as committing insults, defamation, threats, or malicious damage to reputation.
Online product and service providers shall establish and improve early warning, prevention, identification, monitoring, and handling mechanisms for cyberbullying, set up functions and channels that facilitate minors and their guardians to preserve records of cyberbullying incidents and exercise the right to notify, and provide options for cyberbullying information protection that facilitate minors to block unknown users, set the visibility range of their own published information, prohibit reprinting or commenting on their published information, and prohibit the sending of messages to them.
Online product and service providers shall establish and improve a characteristic database of cyberbullying information, optimize relevant algorithm models, and strengthen the identification and monitoring of cyberbullying information by combining technical means such as artificial intelligence and big data with manual review.

Article 27 No organization or individual may organize, instigate, coerce, induce, deceive, or assist minors in committing illegal or criminal acts through the internet in the form of text, images, audio, or video.

Article 28 Online education product and service providers targeting minors shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant provisions of the State, provide corresponding products and services according to the physical and mental development characteristics and cognitive abilities of minors at different age stages.

Article 29 Online product and service providers shall strengthen the management of user-published information and take effective measures to prevent the production, reproduction, publication, or dissemination of information that violates the provisions of Articles 22, 24, 25, the first paragraph of Article 26, and Article 27 of these Regulations. Upon discovering information that violates the provisions of the aforementioned articles, they shall immediately stop transmitting the relevant information, take measures such as deletion, blocking, or disconnection to prevent the spread of the information, preserve relevant records, report to the cyberspace administration, public security, and other departments, and take measures such as warnings, restricting functions, suspending services, or closing accounts against users who produce, reproduce, publish, or disseminate the aforementioned information.
Where an online product or service provider discovers that a user has published or disseminated information specified in the first paragraph of Article 23 of these Regulations without a prominent prompt, it shall provide a prompt or notify the user to provide a prompt; if no prompt is provided, the information shall not be transmitted.

Article 30 Where the national cyberspace administration, news publication, and film departments, and the departments of education, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television under the State Council discover information that violates the provisions of Articles 22, 24, 25, the first paragraph of Article 26, and Article 27 of these Regulations, or discover that information specified in the first paragraph of Article 23 of these Regulations is not provided with a prominent prompt, they shall require the online product or service provider to handle it in accordance with Article 29 of these Regulations; for the aforementioned information originating from outside China, they shall, according to law, notify relevant agencies to take technical measures and other necessary measures to block its dissemination.

Protection of personal information online

Article 31 Where a network service provider provides services such as information publication and instant messaging to minors, it shall, according to law, require the minor or its guardian to provide the minor's true identity information. If the minor or its guardian fails to provide the minor's true identity information, the network service provider shall not provide relevant services to the minor.
An online live streaming service provider shall establish a dynamic verification mechanism for the true identity information of live streamers and shall not provide online live streaming services to minor users who do not meet the circumstances prescribed by law.

Article 32 A personal information processor shall strictly comply with the provisions of the national cyberspace administration department and relevant departments on the scope of necessary personal information for online products and services, and shall not compel minors or their guardians to consent to unnecessary personal information processing acts, and shall not refuse minors to use its basic function services because the minor or their guardian does not consent to the processing of the minor's unnecessary personal information or withdraws consent.

Article 33 A minor's guardian shall educate and guide the minor to enhance awareness and ability of personal information protection, grasp the scope of personal information, understand personal information security risks, and instruct the minor to exercise its rights such as access, reproduction, correction, supplementation, and deletion in the processing of personal information, thereby protecting the minor's rights and interests in personal information.

Article 35 Where a leakage, tampering, or loss of minors' personal information occurs or is likely to occur, the personal information processor shall immediately initiate an emergency response plan for personal information security incidents, take remedial measures, promptly report to the cyberspace administration and other departments, and, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, notify the affected minors and their guardians of the incident by means such as email, letter, telephone, or information push.
If it is difficult to notify the affected individuals one by one, the personal information processor shall promptly issue relevant warning information in a reasonable and effective manner, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations.

Article 36 A personal information processor shall take the principle of least privilege as the basis for its staff, strictly set information access rights, and control the scope of knowledge of minors' personal information. Where a staff member accesses minors' personal information, it shall be approved by the relevant person in charge or its authorized manager, and the access situation shall be recorded, and technical measures shall be taken to avoid illegal processing of minors' personal information.

Article 37 A personal information processor shall, on its own or by entrusting a professional institution, conduct an annual compliance audit on its compliance with laws and administrative regulations in processing minors' personal information, and promptly report the audit situation to the cyberspace administration and other departments.

Article 38 Where a network service provider discovers private information of a minor or personal information published by a minor through the network that involves private information, it shall promptly provide a prompt and take necessary protective measures such as stopping transmission to prevent the spread of the information.
Where a network service provider discovers, through the minor's private information, that the minor may be subjected to infringement, it shall immediately take necessary measures to preserve relevant records and report to the public security organ.

Prevention and intervention of internet addiction

Article 39 The prevention of and intervention in minors' internet addiction shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant provisions of the State.
The departments of education, health, market supervision and administration, and other departments shall, in accordance with their respective functions, exercise supervision and administration over institutions engaged in the prevention of and intervention in minors' internet addiction.

Article 40 Schools shall strengthen the guidance and training of teachers to enhance their ability for early identification and intervention of internet addiction among minor students. For minor students with a tendency towards internet addiction, the school shall promptly inform their guardians and jointly carry out education and guidance with them to help the minor students return to normal study and life.

Article 41 The guardian of a minor shall guide the minor to use the network safely and reasonably, pay attention to the minor's online activities as well as related physiological conditions, psychological conditions, and behavioral habits, prevent the minor from accessing network information that endangers or may affect their physical and mental health, reasonably arrange the time for the minor to use the network, and prevent and intervene in the minor's internet addiction.

Article 42 Network product and service providers shall establish and improve anti-addiction systems, shall not provide products or services that induce minors to become addicted, shall promptly modify content, functions, and rules that may cause minors to become addicted, and shall publicly report on anti-addiction work each year, subject to public supervision.

Article 43 Network service providers such as online games, live streaming, online audio and video, and social networking shall, based on the characteristics of minors of different age groups using their services, adhere to the principles of integration, friendliness, practicality, and effectiveness, set up a minor mode, provide corresponding services in terms of usage periods, duration, functions, and content in accordance with relevant state regulations and standards, and in a conspicuous and convenient manner provide functions such as time management, permission management, and consumption management for guardians to perform their guardianship duties.

Article 44 Network service providers such as online games, live streaming, online audio and video, and social networking shall take measures to reasonably limit the single consumption amount and daily cumulative consumption amount of minors of different age groups when using their services, and shall not provide paid services that are inconsistent with the minor's civil capacity.

Article 45 Network service providers such as online games, live streaming, online audio and video, and social networking shall take measures to prevent and resist harmful value tendencies such as prioritizing traffic, shall not set up online communities, groups, or topics themed on fundraising for fan support, voting for charts, manipulating traffic and controlling reviews, etc., shall not induce minors to participate in online activities such as fundraising for fan support, voting for charts, manipulating traffic and controlling reviews, and shall prevent and stop their users from inducing minors to engage in the above-mentioned acts.

Article 46 Online game service providers shall verify the true identity information of minor users through necessary means such as a unified electronic identity authentication system for minors' online games.
Network product and service providers shall not provide game account rental or sales services for minors.

Article 47 Online game service providers shall establish and improve game rules for preventing minors from becoming addicted to the network, and avoid minors being exposed to game content or game functions that may affect their physical and mental health.
Online game service providers shall implement age-appropriate reminder requirements, classify game products by evaluating elements such as the type, content, and functions of game products based on the physical and mental development characteristics and cognitive abilities of minors of different age groups, clearly indicate the age group of minor users for which the game product is suitable, and provide prominent reminders at locations such as user download, registration, and login interfaces.

Article 48 Departments such as press and publication, education, health, culture and tourism, radio and television, and cyberspace administration shall regularly carry out publicity and education on preventing minors from internet addiction, supervise and inspect network product and service providers' performance of their obligations to prevent minors from internet addiction, and guide families, schools, and social organizations to cooperate with each other to prevent and intervene in minors' internet addiction in a scientific and reasonable manner.
The national press and publication department shall take the lead in organizing and carrying out the prevention and treatment of minors' addiction to online games, and shall, together with relevant departments, formulate administrative regulations on the time periods, duration, and consumption caps for providing online game services to minors.
Health and education departments shall, according to their respective duties, guide relevant medical and health institutions, institutions of higher learning, etc., to carry out basic research on mental disorders and psychological and behavioral problems caused by minors' internet addiction, as well as applied research on screening, assessment, diagnosis, prevention, and intervention.

Article 49 No organization or individual shall intervene in minors' internet addiction or infringe upon minors' lawful rights and interests by means such as abuse or coercion that harm minors' physical and mental health.

Legal Liability

Article 50 Where local people's governments at all levels and relevant departments at or above the county level violate these Regulations and fail to perform their duties on the protection of minors on the network, the superior organ shall order them to make corrections; if they refuse to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, the leading persons directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 51 Where schools, communities, libraries, cultural centers, youth palaces, etc., violate these Regulations and fail to perform their duties on the protection of minors on the network, the education, culture and tourism departments and other relevant departments shall order them to make corrections according to their respective duties; if they refuse to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, the leading persons directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 52 Where a guardian of a minor fails to perform the guardianship duties as provided in these Regulations or infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor, the residents' committee, villagers' committee, women's federation of the minor's place of residence, the guardian's employer, primary and secondary schools, kindergartens, and other units that have close contact with the minor shall, according to law, criticize and educate the guardian, admonish and stop the guardian, and urge the guardian to accept family education guidance, etc.

Article 53 Where the provisions of Article 7, Paragraph 3 of Article 19, or Paragraph 2 of Article 38 of these Regulations are violated, the cyberspace administration, press and publication, film, education, telecommunications, public security, civil affairs, culture and tourism, market supervision and administration, radio and television departments and other relevant departments shall, according to their respective duties, order corrections; if the violator refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons.

Article 54 Where Paragraph 1 of Article 20 of these Regulations is violated, the cyberspace administration, press and publication, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television departments and other relevant departments shall, according to their respective duties, order corrections, give a warning, and confiscate illegal gains; if the violator refuses to make corrections, a concurrent fine of not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons.
Where Subparagraphs 1 and 5 of Paragraph 1 of Article 20 of these Regulations are violated and the circumstances are serious, the cyberspace administration, press and publication, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television departments at or above the provincial level shall, according to their respective duties, order corrections, confiscate illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not more than 50,000,000 yuan or not more than five percent of the previous year's turnover, and may order suspension of relevant businesses or rectification, notify relevant departments to revoke relevant business licenses or revoke business licenses according to law; a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons, and a decision may be made to prohibit them from serving as directors, supervisors, senior officers, or persons in charge of minor protection in relevant enterprises within a certain period.

Article 55 Where the provisions of Article 24 or Article 25 of these Regulations are violated, the cyberspace administration, press and publication, film, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, market supervision and administration, radio and television departments and other relevant departments shall, according to their respective duties, order corrections within a specified period, give a warning, confiscate illegal gains, and may concurrently impose a fine of not more than 100,000 yuan; if the violator refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, it shall be ordered to suspend relevant businesses, stop production or business operations, or revoke relevant business licenses or revoke business licenses. Where illegal gains exceed 1,000,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the illegal gains shall be imposed; where there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 1,000,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 56 Where Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 26, Article 28, Paragraph 1 of Article 29, Paragraph 2 of Article 31, Article 36, Paragraph 1 of Article 38, Articles 42 to 45, Paragraph 2 of Article 46, or Article 47 of these Regulations are violated, the cyberspace administration, press and publication, film, education, telecommunications, public security, culture and tourism, radio and television departments and other relevant departments shall, according to their respective duties, order corrections, give a warning, confiscate illegal gains. Where illegal gains exceed 1,000,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the illegal gains shall be imposed; where there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 1,000,000 yuan, a concurrent fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons; if the violator refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, it may also be ordered to suspend relevant businesses, rectify operations, close the website, revoke relevant business licenses, or revoke the business license.

Article 57 Where a network product or service provider, for violating these Regulations, is subject to a penalty of website closure, revocation of relevant business license, or revocation of business license, it shall not reapply for the relevant license within five years, and its directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons shall not engage in similar network product and service businesses within five years.

Article 58 Where the provisions of these Regulations are violated, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of a minor and causing damage to the minor, civil liability shall be borne according to law; if it constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be given according to law; if it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Supplementary Provisions

Article 59 For the purposes of these Regulations, 'smart terminal products' refer to network terminal products such as mobile phones and computers that can access the network, have an operating system, and allow users to install application software on their own.
Article 60 These Regulations shall come into force on January 1, 2024.
